messages:
Maya L: Heads-up — ACME (enterprise) asked for an "allowlist override" so that their traffic always goes to our 'low-latency' pool and never to the cost-optimized fallback. They want this applied per-org and scoped to specific routes. Can we support this without breaking global routing policies?
Jordan P: Can you paste the exact ask? is it per-route OR global for all their requests? also any duration (permanent vs temporary)?
Maya L: They want it only for model/generate endpoints for now (chat/generate). Permanent for the contract term but needs an admin toggle in console. Also they expect metrics showing how often override was used.
Sahil R: Two major concerns: precedence & quota enforcement. If we route them to a dedicated pool, quotas and SLAs need to follow the override. Also need to ensure we don't bypass denylist protections (e.g., blocked models).
Leah T: UX: Console should expose an "Org routing overrides" page where an admin can add rules: path match, header match (org-id), route target (pool), start/end, and reason. Must be RBAC gated and show audit history.
Maya L: Agree — audit is critical. They specifically asked for header-based override if they set X-Redwood-Org: acme.
Jordan P: Implementation idea: policy engine that evaluates in this order: 1) explicit org override 2) route-level rules (team-defined) 3) global fallback ranking. Overrides are explicit opt-in and require a signed terms flag.
Sahil R: We should keep a safety net: any override cannot disable security checks or model denylist. Also overrides should have an optional token-scope to restrict which keys can use the override.
DevEx Bot: FYI — related support ticket #4861 referenced the same ask, customer mentioned traffic spikes when fallback used.
Leah T: For telemetry, we need new labels: routing.override=true/false, override.type=org_allowlist, override_id, and target_pool. Dashboards: per-org routing effect on latency and cost.
Maya L: How about schema? Draft:
```yaml
- id: "org-acme-low-latency"
  org_id: "acme"
  match:
    path: "/v1/generate*"
    headers:
      X-Redwood-Org: "acme"
  action:
    route_to: "pool-low-latency-us-east-1"
    enforce_quota: true
  enforcement:
    created_by: "maya.l@redwood"
    start_ts: 1763510400
    permanent: true
```
Sahil R: That looks reasonable. Add a `priority` int and `cannot_override_security: true` flag so runtime can short-circuit.
Jordan P: Runtime detail: gateway should evaluate header-based overrides before we run the cost-routing algorithm. But for cached metrics and batching we must ensure we collect per-org batch windows; mixing across pools could corrupt batch targeting.
Maya L: Good call — we should prefer to route entire request to designated pool before batching decisions. That keeps KV cache semantics intact.
Leah T: Rollout plan: feature-flag the console and API endpoints, expose API only to internal admins initially, contract customers via support flow. Canary with 1 customer, measure: error rate, 95p latency, and cost delta.
Sahil R: Tests: unit tests for precedence matrix, integration tests hitting gateway with header variants, and chaos test that simulates pool OOM and confirm automatic fallback to allowed alternatives (but not to cost-opt pool if the override forbids it).
Jordan P: Edge case: what if org override points to a pool that doesn't support model quantization they requested? Need validation: pre-deploy check and a runtime fallback to compatible model variants, plus an admin alert.
Maya L: Logging: include `override_applied` boolean in access logs and `override_reason` string. Put override_id into traces so console can link traces -> override config.
DevEx Bot: Note: existing audit system stores changes in changelog-v2 which will capture console edits. Make sure API edits (org overrides) also create an audit record.
Leah T: UX detail: show a small "Overrides active" badge on per-org usage page with a link to the override config and an explainable summary (who enabled it, when, and the intended effect).
Sahil R: Security review: ensure only org admins with enterprise role can request the change; internal admins must approve self-served toggle. Also require E-signature for permanent overrides >90 days (business rule).
Jordan P: Implementation tasks (proposal):
- gateway: add override evaluation layer (priority + denylist protection)
- policy store: persist override objects (immutable audit entries + mutable active config)
- console: CRUD UI + RBAC checks + audit view
- telemetry: metrics + logs + dashboard panels
- migrations: backfill any existing enterprise exceptions into new schema
- docs + SRE runbook for pool failures
Maya L: Timeline: can we get an internal API + proto + gateway change in 2 sprints? Console follow-up in sprint 3.
Sahil R: Two sprints okay for minimal gates (API + runtime). But need clear acceptance criteria. I'll own the gateway change.
Leah T: I'll spec the console screens and wireframes and pair with DevEx for API docs.
Jordan P: I'll draft the precedence spec and add tests to CI. Also will add telemetry labels to the metrics registry.
Maya L: OK thanks — I'll coordinate with support to pick the canary customer (ACME). Leave a note to Legal for the signed terms for permanent overrides.
OpsBot: deploybot: gateway/override-eval feature-flag created (ff-gateway-org-override), default=false.
Maya L: Thanks all. Recording next steps in the RFC doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/org-routing-overrides (will link when ready).
